summary: Patch special-cases `lookups[0] == 'in'` to collapse a MultiColSource into a single column, which resolves the reported subquery-column-count error but breaks legitimate multi-column relations. For composite/ForeignObject `__in` lookups that genuinely need all target columns, selecting only `targets[0]` yields incorrect filtering.

issues.description: Bypassing MultiColSource for all 'in' lookups is a fragile blanket rule. MultiColSource exists to compare every target column of multi-column foreign relations (ForeignObject/composite FKs); RelatedIn depends on receiving it to split the RHS across columns. Forcing a single `_get_col(targets[0])` silently drops the other join columns, producing wrong results for legitimate multi-column `__in` filters — a correctness break, not just the reported single-column case.

Regression risk for existing composite/multi-column relation filtering: any query relying on MultiColSource + 'in' now compares only the first target column instead of the full tuple. No guard distinguishes the reporter's reverse-m2m case from a genuine multi-column FK.

Fix keys on the exact `'in'` lookup string from the bug report rather than addressing the root cause (why the OR'd path selects all default columns for the related subquery). Reads as a targeted patch to the failing scenario rather than a general fix of the column-selection logic.
Hardcoded `'in'` magic string and terse comment; intent (why only 'in' is safe to collapse) is not explained for future maintainers.
